arxiv-2205-08208.title: Distributed Kalman filtering with event-triggered communication: a robust approach
arxiv-2205-08208.creator: Davide Ghion, Mattia Zorzi
arxiv-2205-08208.description: Abstract We consider the problem of distributed Kalman filtering for sensor networks in the case there is a limit in data transmission and there is model uncertainty. More precisely, we propose a distributed filtering strategy with event-triggered communication in which the state estimators are computed according to the least favorable model.

arxiv-2401-14733.title: Personality Perception in Human Videos Altered by Motion Transfer Networks
arxiv-2401-14733.creator: Ayda Yurtoğlu, Sinan Sonlu, Yalım Doğan, Uğur Güdükbay
arxiv-2401-14733.description: Abstract The successful portrayal of personality in digital characters improves communication and immersion. Current research focuses on expressing personality through modifying animations using heuristic rules or data-driven models. While studies suggest motion style highly influences the apparent personality, the role of appearance can be similarly essential.

arxiv-2412-02716.title: Modelling an electrolyser in a graph-based framework
arxiv-2412-02716.creator: Buu-Van Nguyen, Johan Romate, Cornelis Vuik
arxiv-2412-02716.description: Abstract We propose an electrolyser model for steady-state load flow analysis of multi-carrier energy networks, where the electrolyser is capable of producing hydrogen gas and heat. We show that there are boundary conditions that lead to a well-posed problem. We derive these conditions for two cases, namely with a fixed and non-fixed ratio between gas and heat output.

arxiv-2502-21238.title: The iSWAP gate with polar molecules: Robustness criteria for entangling operations
arxiv-2502-21238.creator: Matteo Bergonzoni, Sven Jandura, Guido Pupillo
arxiv-2502-21238.description: Abstract Ultracold polar molecules trapped in optical lattices or tweezer arrays are an emerging platform for quantum information processing and quantum simulation, thanks to their rich internal structure and long-range dipolar interactions. Recent experimental breakthroughs have enabled precise control over individual molecules, paving the way for implementing two-qubit quantum gates, based on the iSWAP gate.

arxiv-2505-16598.title: How the Shortest and Longest HILDCAAs Shaped Earth’s Outer Radiation Belt During the Van Allen Probes Era?
arxiv-2505-16598.creator: Ayushi Nema, Ankush Bhaskar, Kamlesh N. Pathak, Abhirup Datta
arxiv-2505-16598.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ayushi Nema, Ankush Bhaskar, Kamlesh N. Pathak, Abhirup Datta. High‐intensity long‐duration continuous auroral electrojet (AE) activity (HILDCAA) events are associated with the enhancement of relativistic electron fluxes in the inner magnetosphere. The physical mechanisms underlying this enhancement are not well established yet. In this study, we analyze two contrasting HILDCAA events, one representing the shortest and the other the longest duration, using NASA’s Van Allen Probes observations, which have provided unprecedented, unique in-situ observations of the harsh radiation environment around the Earth.

arxiv-2510-06395.title: A Flux-Tunable Discrete Angular Filter
arxiv-2510-06395.creator: Tristan Lawrie, Oliver M. Brown
arxiv-2510-06395.description: Abstract Recent work by Lawrie et al. [PRR 7, 023209 (2025)] introduced a non-diffracting resonant angular filter on a network of thin channels (modelled via quantum graph theory) that exhibits unit transmission of acoustic waves at a discrete, symmetry-paired set of incidence angles determined solely by the graph topology, while transmission at all other angles is strictly forbidden.

arxiv-2510-13766.title: Are Randomized Quantum Linear Systems Solvers Practical?
arxiv-2510-13766.creator: Siddharth Hariprakash, Roel Van Beeumen, Katherine Klymko, Daan Camps
arxiv-2510-13766.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Siddharth Hariprakash, Roel Van Beeumen, Katherine Klymko, Daan Camps. Randomized quantum algorithms have been proposed in the context of quantum simulation and quantum linear algebra with the goal of constructing shallower circuits than methods based on block encodings. While the algorithmic complexities of such randomized schemes have been shown to be suboptimal, it has been speculated that they may offer benefits in the early fault-tolerant era where circuit depth comes at a premium.

arxiv-2512-07501.title: AutoICE : Automatically Synthesizing Verifiable C Code via LLM-driven Evolution
arxiv-2512-07501.creator: Weilin Luo, Xueyi Liang, Haotian Deng, Yanan Liu, Hai Wan
arxiv-2512-07501.description: Abstract Automatically synthesizing verifiable code from natural language requirements ensures software correctness and reliability while significantly lowering the barrier to adopting the techniques of formal methods. With the rise of large language models (LLMs), long-standing efforts at autoformalization have gained new momentum.

pmc-12387793.title: Nanoscopic Insight into Water Adsorption and Desorption in Commercial Activated Alumina by Positron Annihilation Lifetime Spectroscopy
pmc-12387793.creator: Wojciech Kowalski, Mateusz Kochel, Agnieszka Kierys, Marek Gorgol, Marek Drewniak, Radosław Zaleski
pmc-12387793.description: Activated alumina is widely used in industry as an adsorbent. Its strong affinity toward water allows for the profound dehydration of gas streams. To optimize such processes, a deeper insight into water interaction with activated alumina is required. This knowledge can be obtained using positron annihilation lifetime spectroscopy, a sensitive tool that unravels previously unknown aspects of adsorption processes.

pmc-12595305.title: Collagen fibril formation at the plasma membrane occurs independently from collagen secretion
pmc-12595305.creator: Adam Pickard, Richa Garva, Antony Adamson, Ben C. Calverley, Anna Hoyle, Christina E. Hayward, David Spiller, Yinhui Lu, Nigel Hodson, Oriana Mandolfo, Kevin Kim, George Bou-Gharios, Joe Swift, Brian Bigger, Karl E. Kadler, Alexandra Naba, Tilo Pompe, Mario Raspanti
pmc-12595305.description: BackgroundCollagen fibrils are the primary supporting scaffolds of vertebrate tissues, but the mechanism of assembly is unclear.MethodsHere, using CRISPR-tagging of type I collagen, high-resolution light imaging, and SILAC labelling, we elucidated the cellular mechanism underlying the spatiotemporal assembly of collagen fibrils in cultured fibroblasts.ResultsOur findings reveal the multifaceted trafficking of collagen, including constitutive secretion, intracellular pooling, and plasma membrane-directed fibrillogenesis.

pmc-12621350.title: BAFF in autoimmune kidney diseases: pathogenic pathways, biomarker potential, and therapeutic horizons
pmc-12621350.creator: Jing Wu, Zhaohui Li, Shanshan Zheng, Yipeng Liu, Na Zhao
pmc-12621350.description: Autoimmune kidney diseases usually arise from autoimmune system dysfunction and are characterized by production of autoantibodies. Several autoimmune kidney diseases are currently recognized, including lupus nephritis, antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis, membranous nephropathy, IgA nephropathy. B-cell activating factor (BAFF), a member of the tumor necrosis factor family, serves as a critical regulator of humoral immunity.

pmc-12979523.title: Real-time dynamic graph learning with temporal attention for financial fraud detection
pmc-12979523.creator: Jundong Chen, Yan Yang
pmc-12979523.description: Financial transaction risk control is a cornerstone of intelligent finance platforms, yet existing approaches remain limited. Early frameworks modeled user behaviors independently, while later graph-based systems extracted handcrafted features from capital-flow networks. Although these methods improved detection, they struggle to capture fine-grained temporal dynamics and evolving topological patterns, and they depend heavily on manual feature engineering.
